`MaxToolCallsPerTurn` and the content-free audit count it. Mark a tool that opens a form for a change
with `HandsOffChange()`: it is offered only where the agent's model is offered changes in a person's
chat (execute autonomy), exactly where it could propose the same change, and its description tells the
model to prefer the hand-off over a proposal while the person takes part. Keep proposals for runs,
consultations and changes the person should approve rather than make.

A turn offers a client tool only in a person's own chat whose browser declared its handler; agent
threads, runs, rule turns, consultations, an application's channel (`INhAssistantConversationTurns`),
follow-up turns, a step of a composition or script, and MCP clients never get one, and a call there
ends at once as `not-executed` with `assistant-client-tool-unavailable`, without running anything.
When the model calls it, the invoker authorizes and audits the call and the turn waits as for a
question: the call is `awaiting-client`, the conversation `waiting-for-approval` with
`pendingClientTool`, and only the stream of the person's own request receives `client-tool.requested`
with the bound `arguments`; other sessions and participants see the waiting call without them. The
person's browser runs the handler and posts the result to `POST
conversations/{id}/client-tools/{invocationId}/result` (`NhAssistantClientToolResultRequest`): a
`status` of `completed`, `declined`, `unavailable` or `failed`, a dash-case `outcome` such as `saved`,
an optional `id` of what the person created, and `data` only for a tool that declares
`Returns<TResult>()`, which is bound to `TResult` so undeclared properties never reach the model. Anyone
else is refused with `403 assistant-client-tool-forbidden`, a call that no longer waits with
`409 assistant-client-tool-not-pending` and a result out of bounds with `400
assistant-client-tool-result-invalid`. The result resumes the turn as a stream with the report as the
call's output, data from the browser and never instructions; the turn continues on the tool calls,
tokens and consultations it has left. The wait ends after `NhAssistantLimits.ClientToolLifetime` (15
minutes by default, one minute to one day) on the application's clock: a late result is refused with
`409 assistant-client-tool-expired` and releases the conversation, as a new message does, and stopping
the turn cancels the call. The audit records `ClientToolRequested`, `ClientToolCompleted` with the
reported status and `ClientToolExpired`, never the arguments, the outcome, the id or the data. A
client tool needs no storage of its own: it lives in its call and the message's `client-tool` part.

## Application messages

The application posts its own messages into a conversation with
`INhAssistantConversationMessages.PostAsync(conversationId, message)`, for example when a
long-running export that a person started from the chat has finished. It is a server-side API for the
application's code; clients have no endpoint to post such messages. It works for people's chat
conversations and for agent threads alike:

```csharp
var posted = await messages.PostAsync(conversationId, new NhAssistantApplicationMessage(
    $"The portfolio analysis of **{NhAssistantMarkdown.Escape(divisionName)}** finished with **12 projects**.")
{
    // The conversation id came from the person's client: post only when that person may open it.
    Access = NhAssistantApplicationMessageAccess.ReadableBy(new NhAssistantConversationPerson(ownerActorId)),
    Title = "Portfolio analysis finished",
    SenderName = "Portfolio analysis",
    Link = new NhAssistantApplicationMessageLink($"/background-operations/{operationId}", "Open the analysis"),
    Notify = true,
    // A retried background step posts once.
    IdempotencyKey = "portfolio-analysis:" + operationId.ToString("N")
}, cancellationToken);
```

- Every message makes the access choice `Access`, which the compiler requires:
  `NhAssistantApplicationMessageAccess.ReadableBy(person)` posts only when that person may open the
  conversation now, otherwise `assistant-conversation-not-found` and nothing is stored, shown or
  notified: a chat as its owner or as a participant of the same tenant, an agent thread by the live
  read rule, so with a live role on its subject or an invitation to it and never through a participant
  row left from an earlier role, never in a shadow thread or a thread of a shadow variant, and only
  in the person's tenant or the whole application they take part in. Choose it whenever a client
  named the conversation.
  `NhAssistantApplicationMessageAccess.WithoutPersonCheck()` posts into any conversation that is not
  archived; choose it only for a conversation the application chose itself, such as the thread of
  an agent it runs. A message whose `Access` is null anyway is `assistant-message-invalid`.
- The text is Markdown, as the chat renders the agent's answers, within `MaxMessageChars`
  (`assistant-message-too-long`). Put data people entered, such as a project or division name, into
  it with `NhAssistantMarkdown.Escape`: it backslash-escapes the ASCII punctuation Markdown may give a
  meaning and drops indentation at the start of a line, so the name shows as it is and keeps its line
  breaks. Escape running text, headings and link text, not code spans, code blocks or link addresses.
  Title (200), sender (100), idempotency key (100) and link label (100) are single lines shown as
  plain text; the link is a path within the application or an absolute `https` address. Anything
  else is `assistant-message-invalid`.
- An unknown or archived conversation is `assistant-conversation-not-found`.
- The message gets role `application` (`NhAssistantMessageRoles.Application`) and the next sequence
  number, so it is unread for the conversation's people and moves the conversation up in their lists.
  They see it at once through the live `message.created` event and in every snapshot, with
  `authorKind: application` and `application` (`NhAssistantApplicationMessageDto`: title, sender
  name, link and `trusted`).
- `Notify` adds a Web Push notification of kind `application-message` to the owner and participants
  of a chat, or the participants of an agent thread; it carries the conversation's title and a fixed
  text, never the message. When the application turned on `UseInAppAgentNotifications`, the same
  people also get an in-app message through `INhUserNotificationSink` (a warning is logged without
  one): category `assistant-application`, one `GroupKey` per conversation, the conversation's title
  and a fixed text in the recipient's culture from `INhActorDirectory` (otherwise the current UI
  culture), never the message; actor ids that are no user id are skipped. A shadow thread never
  notifies.
- A repeated post with the same `IdempotencyKey` posts, notifies and audits nothing and returns the
  earlier message with `Duplicate`.
- The audit records `ApplicationMessagePosted` with the message id, `posted` or `notified` (by
  either channel), `ApplicationMessageTrusted` and, in a thread, its subject; never the text, title,
  link or sender.
- A later turn gives the message to the model as a user message that starts with `[Application]`,
  says that it is information from the application, not a request from the people in the
  conversation and never instructions, and holds the sender, title, link and text in an
  `application-message` block whose content cannot close it. Write it as information.
  Conversation snapshots for reviewed MCP tools leave every application message out.
- `Trusted = true` makes the model follow the message as the application's instruction: the same
  marker and block, with a sentence that the application, not the people in the conversation, gives
  this instruction. The flag is stored with the message (no migration) and audited, and people see
  it: `NhAssistantApplicationMessageDto.Trusted` (JSON `trusted`, `false` for any other message) in
  snapshots and the live `message.created` event, which `nh-assistant-thread` shows as the label
  "Instruction for the assistant". **Never put user-generated data into a trusted message**: no names, descriptions, comments,
  file names or anything else people or other systems entered, not even escaped with
  `NhAssistantMarkdown.Escape`, because the model would follow instructions hidden in it. Write
  trusted text entirely in code or from the application's own configuration.

SampleProjectManagement's portfolio analysis tells the conversation that started it when it
finished (SPM-312, `ProjectAnalysisAssistantNotices`): `ReadableBy` the person who started it, the
division's name escaped, untrusted because of that name, by Web Push and in its test host's inbox,
followed by a trusted instruction for the assistant in fixed text without people's data. Started with
the id of a project's agent thread, it tells a person whose role on the project ended nothing there,
also after they opened the thread before, and the project's owner, who may read it now, everything.

## A person's turns through the application's channels

When a person talks with the assistant outside the client, such as in a messaging app, the
application sends their message and decides their approval with `INhAssistantConversationTurns`
instead of calling its own HTTP endpoints. It is a server API; the application vouches for the
person, as for `INhAssistantProposalDecisionService`: it authenticated them through its channel and
passes their principal and actor id, and their tenant, as `NhAssistantDecidingPerson`:

```csharp
var sent = await turns.SendAsync(
    // The tenant the person signs in with; null only in a host without tenants.
    new NhAssistantDecidingPerson(principal, userId.ToString("D"), tenantId),
    conversationId,
    new NhAssistantConversationMessage(text) { ClientMessageId = deliveryId },
    new NhAssistantConversationTurnOptions("messaging-chat")
    {
        // As the active-division header of the person's own request would name it.
        ActiveDivisionId = divisionId,
        // The provider's webhook may give up; the chat then holds the answer.
        KeepTurnAfterCallerLeaves = true
    },
    cancellationToken);
if (sent.Success && sent.Data!.PendingApprovals.FirstOrDefault() is { } approval)
{
    // Later, when the person answers the approval card:
    await turns.DecideAsync(
        person,
        conversationId,
        approval.ApprovalId,
        new NhAssistantConversationDecision(NhAssistantProposalDecision.Approve, approval.ProposalHash),
        new NhAssistantConversationTurnOptions("messaging-chat") { ActiveDivisionId = divisionId },
        cancellationToken);
}
```

When the channel can show activity, pass `NhAssistantConversationTurnOptions.Progress`, an
`IProgress<NhAssistantTurnProgress>`, so its client sees the turn work instead of silence, which feels
faster even when nothing is. Each step has a `Kind` from `NhAssistantTurnProgressKinds`: `started`,
`text` with the new text, `tool-started` and `tool-completed` with `NhAssistantTurnProgressTool`, and
`ended` with the status and code. A step carries a tool's id, name and outcome, never its arguments or
result. A handler that throws is logged once and asked no further, so it never stops the turn. Text
arrives per fragment of the model's stream, so a channel such as MCP does better with one progress
notification per tool and a few for the text.

A channel whose caller has a time limit, such as an MCP tool, lets the turn outlive it with
`KeepTurnAfterCallerLeaves` and reads the answer later with `WaitAsync` instead of polling
`INhAssistantConversations.GetAsync`:

```csharp
var waited = await turns.WaitAsync(
    person,
    conversationId,
    new NhAssistantTurnWait(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(40)) { Language = language, Progress = progress },
    cancellationToken);
if (waited.Success && waited.Data!.Status == NhAssistantTurnStatuses.Running)
{
    // The bound passed first: tell the client to ask again. The turn goes on.
}
```

- `WaitAsync` returns the result of `SendAsync` once the chat's turn ended or waits for a person,
  whoever started it, or status `running` without a message when `Timeout` passes first. A chat without
  a running turn answers at once, so `TimeSpan.Zero` only reads the state. The wait neither cancels the
  turn nor keeps it alive, and the caller's cancellation throws `OperationCanceledException` and leaves
  the turn alone.
- It applies the checks of a turn, and reads the conversation at an interval while it waits, so access
  that ends also ends the wait with `assistant-conversation-not-found`, and a turn on another host is
  seen too. Only a turn on this host reports progress and the status, code, usage and timings of its end.
  A turn that ended earlier or elsewhere is read from the conversation, which keeps no outcome per turn:
  status `completed`, `waiting-for-approval` or `failed`, so a cancelled turn reads as `completed` and a
  failed one has no code.
- `NhAssistantConversationTurnResult.Timings` (`NhAssistantTurnTimings`) says where the time of a turn
  went, and the turn's log line says the same: total, preparation with its MCP, retrieval and file parts,
  model time and calls, tool time and the time to the first text. Read it before changing anything for
  speed: a turn's own work takes milliseconds, and its wait is nearly always the model, its reasoning
  effort (`WithReasoning`), or a tool or MCP server.

- A turn is the endpoint's turn, through the same runner and with the same rules: the person's
  conversation (the owner, or a participant of the same tenant), the assistant's access policy and
  the agent's own policy (`assistant-agent-forbidden`), the message limits, the approval rules and the
  person's own rights for every tool. Only chats are served; an agent's thread answers
  `assistant-conversation-not-found`.
- The person's invocation context comes from the application's
  `INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver`, run over a request that carries only the principal.
  When it refuses the principal, or resolves another actor id or tenant than the person names, the
  call fails with `assistant-context-unavailable`: the application cannot act in one person's
  conversation with another person's rights. `ActiveDivisionId` counts as the request header does:
  only when the host maps the active division and the person passes its policy; division policies
  then read it from the authorization resource, which implements `INhDivisionScopedResource`.
- The turn runs without the caller's request and in services of its own that end with the turn. Its
  tools authorize the person, never the request around the call: a webhook's or another person's
  request lends no principal and no credential. API bridge tools, which forward the person's own
  request credential, are not offered, and MCP servers that forward the person's sign-in are not
  reached.
- `SendAsync`, `DecideAsync` and `AnswerAsync` return `NhAssistantConversationTurnResult` once the
  turn ended or waits: its status (`completed`, `waiting-for-approval`, `cancelled`, `failed`), the
  error code, the assistant's message as the conversation shows it, the pending approvals with their
  proposal hash, the question it waits for (`PendingQuestion`) and the usage. Expected refusals before
  the turn are failed results with the endpoint's codes; a repeated `ClientMessageId` is
  `assistant-message-duplicate`.
- A channel that knows the page the person has open, such as a website widget, passes it as
  `ClientContext` of the message, in the endpoint's `NhAssistantClientContextDto`:
  `new NhAssistantConversationMessage(text) { ClientContext = new NhAssistantClientContextDto(route,
  title, [new NhAssistantClientEntityDto("project", projectId, label)]) }`. The service reads it as the
  endpoint reads `clientContext`, so the turn shows the same "User's screen", the message stores the
  same context and a resumed turn shows it again. Unlike the endpoint, which ignores what it cannot
  read so that a browser's message never fails for its page, the service refuses with
  `assistant-message-invalid` a page the endpoint would not keep whole: a route without text, more
  than five entities, an entity that is `null`, whose type is not dash-case or whose id is empty,
  longer than 64 characters or holds a control character, and a page whose stored form exceeds the
  4,000 characters the message keeps for it, which the endpoint ignores. Long text is cut off as the endpoint does. The page is
  untrusted data for the model and grants nothing.
- An application that serves its channel through its own API answers a failed result with the
  status the endpoints give its code: map the application's own codes first, then
  `NhAssistantHttpStatuses.Of(code)`, which answers `400` (`UnknownCodeStatus`) for a code the
  assistant does not know. The endpoints use the same mapping, so a channel and the endpoints answer a
  code alike.
- `AnswerAsync(person, conversationId, questionId, new NhAssistantConversationAnswer(choice), options)`
  answers the question with the zero-based choice in the answer endpoint's order: an unknown question
  `assistant-question-not-found`, another person's `assistant-question-forbidden` (before the status),
  one that no longer waits `assistant-question-not-pending`, a choice outside it
  `assistant-question-answer-invalid` and an expired one `assistant-question-expired`, which closes it
  and releases the chat. The rest of the turn runs with the rights of the person who answered.
- The caller's cancellation throws `OperationCanceledException` and cancels the turn, unless
  `KeepTurnAfterCallerLeaves` lets it run on up to `TurnTimeout`; `null` follows
  `KeepTurnsAfterDisconnect`.
- The audit records the channel (`NhAssistantAuditEvent.Channel`) on the turn's events, such as
  `ToolInvoked`, `ApprovalRequested` and `ApprovalApproved`; the endpoints' turns record none.

`INhAssistantConversations` creates, lists, reads and stops the person's chat, lists the agents the
person may chat with and uploads a file to a chat for the same channels, with the checks and codes of
`POST conversations`, `GET conversations`, `GET conversations/{id}`, `POST conversations/{id}/cancel`,
`GET agents` and `POST conversations/{id}/files`, which audit none of them:

```csharp
var created = await conversations.CreateAsync(
    person,
    new NhAssistantNewConversation("project-assistant") { Title = "Launch project" },
    new NhAssistantConversationOptions { ActiveDivisionId = divisionId },
    cancellationToken);
var chat = await conversations.GetAsync(person, created.Data!.Id, options, cancellationToken);
await conversations.CancelAsync(person, created.Data!.Id, options, cancellationToken);
var chats = await conversations.ListAsync(person, new NhAssistantConversationPage(Page: 1, ItemsPerPage: 10), options, cancellationToken);
var agents = await conversations.ListAgentsAsync(person, options, cancellationToken);
// The delivered attachment, readable again: the content check, the scanner and the file source read it.
await using var content = attachment.OpenReadStream();
var uploaded = await conversations.UploadAsync(
    person,
    created.Data!.Id,
    new NhAssistantConversationUpload(attachment.FileName, attachment.ContentType, content),
    options,
    cancellationToken);
// The person's next message carries the reference.
await turns.SendAsync(
    person,
    created.Data!.Id,
    new NhAssistantConversationMessage(text) { Files = [uploaded.Data!] },
    new NhAssistantConversationTurnOptions("messaging-chat"),
    cancellationToken);
```

- `CreateAsync` starts an empty chat in the person's tenant with an agent offered in the chat:
  `assistant-agent-not-found` otherwise, `assistant-title-invalid` above 200 characters and
  `assistant-agent-forbidden` without the access or the agent's policy. `GetAsync` returns the
  endpoint's `NhAssistantConversationDto`, with the share token for the owner; a participant must also
  pass the agent's policy. `CancelAsync` stops the running turn in this process, or rejects the
  waiting approval and cancels the waiting question; only the owner or the person who started the
  turn may (`assistant-turn-forbidden`), and the agent's policy is not checked.
- `ListAsync` returns the endpoint's `NhAssistantConversationListDto`: the chats the person owns or
  takes part in, most recently updated first, with the person's read state, never an agent's thread;
  `NhAssistantConversationPage` takes a page from 1 and 1 to 100 chats (`assistant-message-invalid`
  otherwise, 20 without one). `ListAgentsAsync` returns the agents of `GET agents` with their
  `Uploads`. Both share their code with the endpoints, so a channel lists what the panel lists.
- `UploadAsync` is the upload endpoint's call without the multipart request: after the chat, the
  agent's policy for everyone who uploads (the owner too, since uploading belongs to starting a turn),
  a file source, an agent that accepts files and whose profile chain may receive them, then the name,
  the type against the content, the size, the scanner and the file source, each with the endpoint's
  code. `NhAssistantConversationUpload.Content` must be readable and seekable: the call reads it from
  its current position again for each step and leaves it open for the caller, who disposes it; a
  stream that cannot seek throws `ArgumentException`. Buffer a network stream first, within the
  agent's `MaxFileBytes`. The file's name is never logged. The returned `NhAiFileReference` goes into
  `NhAssistantConversationMessage.Files` of the person's next message.
- Each call resolves the person as the turns do (`assistant-context-unavailable`), checks the
  assistant's access policy with the person's resource (`assistant-agent-forbidden`) and serves chats
  only: an agent's thread answers `assistant-conversation-not-found`. It runs without the caller's
  request, in services of its own and in the culture of `NhAssistantConversationOptions.Language`.

SampleProjectManagement's messaging channel (SPM-332, `SampleAssistantMessagingChannel`) links a chat
for the signed-in person, rebuilds the person from the user store for every delivery and runs the
turn in their active division; a repeated delivery starts no second turn and a link to someone else's
chat finds nothing. A link is a credential of the person: issue it only from the person's own session
(an impersonation session gets `403 assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating`), bind it to the
person's security stamp so that a password change or session revocation ends it, and let a chat
started through it inherit its expiry instead of a fresh lifetime. SPM-341 starts a chat with another
agent from the messaging app, reads the linked chat, answers its question card by the choice's number
or text and stops its turn. SPM-358 lists the person's chats, each with a link token of its own that
expires with the presented link, and the agents with what the person may attach, and uploads the
provider's attachment to the linked chat with the upload endpoint's codes and statuses. SPM-342 names the
turn's person in the situation from `INhAiTurnPerson`, tells the model it answers in the messaging app
from `Channel`, and stamps `ConversationId` and `Channel` on the status event a tool publishes.
SPM-380 lets the provider's web widget on a portal page send the page the person has open with the
message, which reaches the model as the person's screen through `ClientContext`; a page the platform
would not keep whole answers `400 assistant-message-invalid`. SPM-381 answers every refusal of the
channel with `SampleAssistantMessagingChannel.StatusOf`: the channel's own codes first, then
`NhAssistantHttpStatuses.Of`, so the messaging app keeps no table of its own.

## A chat about a subject

A person may start a chat about one subject, such as the project whose page they have open. Name it
when the chat is created: `subjectType` and `subjectId` of `POST conversations`, or
`NhAssistantNewConversation.Subject` of `INhAssistantConversations.CreateAsync`. An agent that only
makes sense about a subject says so with `RequireChatSubject()`:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    .AddAgent(projectChat)
    .ConfigureAgent("project-chat", run => run
        // The chat's subject must be something the agent works on.
        .WorksOn("project")
        // Left out of GET agents and the status; offered for chats about a project only.
        .RequireChatSubject()));

var subject = new NhAiSubjectRef("project", projectId.ToString("D"));
var agents = await conversations.ListAgentsAsync(person, subject, options, cancellationToken);
var created = await conversations.CreateAsync(
    person,
    new NhAssistantNewConversation("project-chat") { Subject = subject },
    options,
    cancellationToken);
```

- Creating checks the subject with its access resolver, the tenant and what the agent works on or,
  for a chat-only agent, chats about (`ChatsAbout`):
  `assistant-subject-invalid` (400) for one of `subjectType` and `subjectId` without the other, an
  invalid id or a type of the platform (a chat without a subject is already about the whole
  application), `assistant-subject-type-unknown` (404) for a type without a resolver,
  `assistant-subject-not-found` (404) when the resolver does not describe it or the person's tenant
  does not reach it, `assistant-subject-access-denied` (403) when the resolver gives the person no
  role on it (`Reader` is enough: the chat's tools run with the person's own rights), and
  `assistant-agent-does-not-work-on` (409) when neither the agent's `WorksOn` nor its `ChatsAbout`
  covers it. An agent with `RequireChatSubject()` refuses a chat without a subject with
  `assistant-subject-required` (400).
- The resolver is asked again on every turn (a message, a decision and an answer, through the
  endpoints and `INhAssistantConversationTurns` alike, which also check that the agent still works on
  the subject), read (`GET conversations/{id}`, marking read, uploads, `GetAsync` and `UploadAsync`),
  invitation (joining through a link, inviting from the directory, whose candidates list only people
  with a role) and delivery without a request (live updates, Web Push, in-app notifications and an
  application message `ReadableBy` the person), for the owner as for the participants and in the
  chat's tenant. Revoked access takes effect at once; deleting, leaving, stopping a turn, revoking the
  link and removing people stay possible. The conversation list shows `subject` with the name stored
  when the chat was created and asks no resolver.
- The turn offers the subject without making the chat the agent's thread: tools, turn context
  providers and retrieval read `NhAiInvocationContext.ConversationSubject`; a proposal guard reads
  `NhAiProposalGuardContext.ConversationSubject` at the proposal stage, while `Subject` keeps naming
  where a proposal waits (none in a chat); the file source reads `NhAssistantFileActor.ConversationSubject`
  for uploads and opened files, and still opens them for the person; the subject type's briefing
  provider is asked with `NhAssistantBriefingPurposes.Chat`, after a section that names the subject. The
  chat shares no memory, run, proposal or member with the agent's thread about the subject, and the
  subject's approvers do not decide its proposals; the person does, inline.
- `GET agents` and the status leave out agents that require a subject; `GET agents?subjectType=&subjectId=`
  and `ListAgentsAsync(person, subject)` list the agents that work on the subject and the chat-only
  agents that chat about its type (`ChatOnly().ChatsAbout(types)`, see the agent runs rule), those that
  require one included, after the same checks as creating. `RequireChatSubject()` is a setting in code;
  the host refuses to start for a chat-only agent (`ChatOnly()`) without `ChatsAbout` and next to
  `HideFromChat()`. Chats that exist without a subject keep working.
- `INhAiSubjectRetention.ForgetSubjectAsync(subject, scopeKey)` deletes the chats about the subject in
  that scope with their messages, and the application's file retention forgets their uploads with the
  reason `subject-forgotten`. The subject's columns and index on `AssistantConversation` come with the
  migration `ChatSubject` on SQL Server and PostgreSQL; hosts must apply it.

SampleProjectManagement's project chat (SPM-363, `SampleProjectChatComposition`) works on projects and
requires a subject; the project dialog starts it with `NhAssistantStore.setChatSubject`. A reader of the
project chats with the project's briefing, someone of another division is refused, and a member removed
from the project can no longer read or continue the chat but still deletes it. The same dialog starts a
chat about the project with the chat helper of SPM-343, which chats about projects without working on
them (`ChatOnly().ChatsAbout(ProjectSubjects.Type)`).

## Files in model turns

Let turns read the application's files with `UseFileSource<T>()`, where `T` implements
`INhAssistantFileSource`. The application keeps the files, decides who may read them and how
sensitive they are; the assistant keeps references and hashes only. Without a source turns take no
files, and every file is refused with `assistant-files-unavailable`. Declare on the model profile
which media types its model reads itself, and give the files people upload, which are
`Confidential` by default, a fallback profile that permits them:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapPlatformAI(ai => ai
    .AddChatProfile("project-assistant-chat", profile => profile
        .UseKeyedClient("project-model")
        .RequireCapabilities(NhAiModelCapability.FunctionCalling)
        .WithStreaming(NhAiStreamingPolicy.Allowed)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal)
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg)
        .WithFallbackProfiles("project-assistant-confidential"))
    .AddChatProfile("project-assistant-confidential", profile => profile
        .UseKeyedClient("confidential-model")
        .RequireCapabilities(NhAiModelCapability.FunctionCalling)
        .WithStreaming(NhAiStreamingPolicy.Allowed)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal, NhAiDataClassification.Confidential)
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg)));

services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .WithLimits(limits => { limits.MaxFilesPerTurn = 3; }));
```

SampleProjectManagement implements the source on its media library (SPM-305): uploads live in a
folder of their conversation and open only in its turns, a project document opens for the people who
see the project's agent work and for an agent on that project, and the media library's own endpoints
never serve the uploads.

- `OpenAsync(reference, actor, cancellationToken)` returns `TaskResult<NhAssistantFile>` with the
  content stream, media type, length, page count where known and the file's
  `NhAiDataClassification`. Check that `actor` may read the file now: the person of a chat turn, or
  in a run the agent with the initiator and accountable owner it works for
  (`NhAssistantFileActor`). Return `assistant-file-not-found` or `assistant-file-forbidden`
  otherwise. `StoreUploadAsync` stores a file a person uploads to a conversation in the
  application's own storage and returns its reference; return a failed result for a type, size or
  scan outcome the application refuses.
- A tool names files in its result through data that implements `INhAiToolResultFiles` (mark the
  property `[JsonIgnore]`) or with `NhAiToolResult.Create(result, options, files)`. The result
  then carries `files` next to `data`: each `NhAiFileReference` with id, name, media type, size
  and hash, never content. The assistant opens every file through the source with the turn's actor,
  so a tool cannot hand the model a file that actor may not read.
- When the profile that serves the turn declares the media type, the model reads the file itself:
  it follows the tool results as file content in a user message, behind a marker that names it as
  external data that is never instructions. Nothing in a file changes the tools, rights or
  approvals of the turn. A type the profile does not declare goes to a reading tool (below);
  without one it is refused with `assistant-file-type-not-supported`, which names the type.
- A reading tool turns a type the model cannot read into text. Register the application's own
  with `AddFileReader<T>(readerId, reader => reader.AcceptMediaTypes(...).PermitDataClassifications(...))`,
  where `T` implements `INhAssistantFileReader` and returns `TaskResult<string>` for an
  `NhAssistantFileReadRequest` (reference, media type, content, classification, actor). A reader
  permits `Public` and what it declares, as a model profile does. The readers an administrator set
  up on MCP servers follow (see the MCP bullets). The readers of the application come first in
  registration order, then the MCP readers by priority, highest first, then by server id and tool
  name; the first that accepts the type and permits the file's classification reads it. A reader that may not receive the file is passed over, and when
  none may, the code of the first one that declares the type applies, such as
  `assistant-classification-not-permitted`. The model reads the text behind the same marker, as
  untrusted external data. A reader that received the file and failed, threw or returned no text
  refuses it with `assistant-file-reader-failed` (`502`); the file never goes to a second reader and
  the reader's messages never reach the model, the person or the log.
- The limits count a reader's text, one token per started four characters, instead of pages: a
  file is sent to a reader only while the turn has room for its text, and text beyond
  `MaxFileTokensPerTurn` or the profile's input budget is refused with `assistant-file-token-limit`.
  Every reader learns that budget beforehand as `NhAssistantFileReadRequest.MaxTextCharacters`, four
  characters to each token left. The file's own bytes and pages still count against `MaxFileBytes`
  and `MaxFilePages`.
- The result names per file whether the model received it (`attached` with the SHA-256 of what it
  read as `hash`) or the `code` and `message` of its refusal; the tool call itself succeeds.
- `NhAssistantLimits` bounds every file and turn: `MaxFileBytes` (20 MB), `MaxFilePages` (100,
  when the source reports a page count), `MaxFilesPerTurn` (5; the files of one result count
  together) and `MaxFileTokensPerTurn` (100,000; a file counts 1,000 tokens per page, an image
  one page and a file without a page count one page per started 100 KB, also within the profile's
  input budget). Each refusal has its own code: `assistant-file-too-large`,
  `assistant-file-too-many-pages`, `assistant-file-count-limit` and `assistant-file-token-limit`.
  An agent or skill can only lower them (`AcceptsFiles(limits => ...)`, `NhAssistantFileLimits`, or
  the lower limits an administrator stores with the agent's run settings and a data skill).
- The turn takes the highest classification of its files, its agent and its skill. A model call
  that carries a more sensitive file goes to the fallback profile that permits it; a file no profile
  of the chain may receive is refused with `assistant-classification-not-permitted`.
- The chat assistant, an agent without run settings, accepts files at once. An agent configured
  with `ConfigureAgent`, and each of its skills, accepts none until it is switched on with
  `AcceptsFiles()` or in the administration; see the agent-runs rule. Otherwise files are refused
  with `assistant-files-not-accepted`.
- Messages and tool calls keep the reference, name, media type and hashes of a file, never its
  content. A later turn opens the files of the history it replays again through the source with its
  own actor, newest first and each file once, within the same limits on their own; a file it cannot
  open is named in its place with the reason.
- Opening files before the model loop (a person's attachments, the files of messages that waited for
  a run and the earlier files a turn opens again) follows the turn's cancellation and ends at
  `NhAssistantLimits.TurnTimeout`, in every kind of turn: a file source or reader that accepts the
  request and never answers ends the turn with `assistant-turn-timeout` and releases the thread and
  the run's worker, and a person's or an administrator's stop ends it cancelled. Pass the
  `cancellationToken` of `OpenAsync` and `ReadAsync` to every call that can wait.
- The one exception: a conversation keeps the text a reading tool made of a file, so a later turn
  does not send the same document to the reader again. The text is keyed by the SHA-256 of the
  content the reader received and the reader, protected with ASP.NET Data Protection (share the key
  ring between instances), kept for `NhAssistantLimits.ReaderTextRetention` (24 hours by default, at
  most 30 days; `TimeSpan.Zero` keeps none) and removed with its conversation. Every later turn still
  opens the file through the source with its own actor, so access and classification are checked
  again; a changed file has another hash, and a reader the turn would no longer choose, or may no
  longer send the file to, gets nothing from it. A kept text is read instead of calling the reader.
- `FileRead` and `FileRefused` business events carry `FileId`, `FileName`, `FileMediaType`,
  `FileHash`, how the file reached the turn as `ObjectId` (`NhAssistantFileOrigins`) and, for a
  tool result, the tool and invocation. `FileName` is the reference's name, at most 256 characters,
  without control, format or separator characters and in Unicode normalization form C: the only free
  text of the event. `FileReaderId` names the reading tool that read, refused or failed the file:
  the reader id, or `mcp.<server>` with `McpConnectionOwner` for an MCP server; for a file a reader
  read, `FileHash` is the SHA-256 of the content the reader received and `FileTextCached` says whether
  the text was the conversation's kept text. File content and a reader's text never reach logs,
  audit or usage records, and the file's name stays out of logs.

A reading tool of the application, registered next to the file source. NewHeap's packages carry no
document library; the sample's `OfficeDocumentReader` (SPM-305) is an example to copy, which reads
Word and Excel documents with DocumentFormat.OpenXml in the application's own process:

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .AddFileReader<OfficeDocumentReader>("office-documents", reader => reader
        .AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Docx, NhAiMediaTypes.Xlsx)
        .PermitDataClassifications(NhAiDataClassification.Internal, NhAiDataClassification.Confidential)));
```

- Bound what a reader unpacks, such as OpenXml's `OpenSettings.MaxCharactersInPart`, and return a
  failed result for a damaged document instead of text cut off; the turn's limits count the text.
- A part bound is no bound on the text: cells can name one shared string again and again, and
  several sheets can name one worksheet, so the text can be far longer than the file. Bound the
  text while it is made, value by value, by `NhAssistantFileReadRequest.MaxTextCharacters`, the
  characters the turn can still take, and stop with a failed result with
  `NhAssistantErrorCodes.FileTokenLimit`, which refuses the file with `assistant-file-token-limit`;
  read each part once and check the `cancellationToken` at every row or paragraph. MCP readers get
  the same budget host-side: a longer text is refused before its blocks are joined.

People attach files to a chat message in two steps. First the client uploads each file to the
conversation with `POST {prefix}/conversations/{id}/files`: `multipart/form-data` with one file part
named `file` and the header `X-NH-Assistant-Upload: 1`, which a cross-site form cannot send, so the
endpoint keeps the posture of the JSON endpoints under the same access policy. The endpoint checks, in
this order, the conversation and the agent's policy (as for a message), a file source
(`assistant-files-unavailable`), an agent that accepts files (`assistant-files-not-accepted`), one
named, non-empty file part (`assistant-file-upload-invalid`), an accepted media type whose content
starts as files of that type do (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`), the agent's `MaxFileBytes`
(`assistant-file-too-large`) and, when the application registered one, its upload scanner
(`INhAssistantUploadScanner` with `ConfigureUploads(uploads => uploads.UseScanner<T>())`): a file it
refuses answers `assistant-file-scan-refused` (422), a scan that could not run
(`assistant-file-upload-failed` from the scanner, or an exception) answers
`assistant-file-upload-failed` (503), and nothing is stored; without a scanner nothing is scanned.
Only then does `StoreUploadAsync` receive the file, with the name
without its path, the media type lowercase and `NhAssistantFileUpload.Classification`; it answers the
`NhAiFileReference` the endpoint returns. A refusal of the source answers
`assistant-file-upload-refused` (422) unless it is `assistant-file-too-large`,
`assistant-file-type-not-accepted` or `assistant-files-unavailable`; an exception or an invalid
reference answers `assistant-file-upload-failed` (503) and logs only its type. Then the message carries
the references in `files` of `POST conversations/{id}/messages` (`NhAssistantSendMessageRequest.Files`),
at most the agent's files per turn, and the turn opens them as described above.

Browsers send no media type, or a generic one, for files their system does not know, and Windows
names some extensions after the program that opens them, such as `application/vnd.ms-excel` for a
`.csv` file. A file part without a type, with `application/octet-stream` (or
`binary/octet-stream`, `application/unknown`) or with such a type for its extension therefore takes
the type its file name's extension names, but only a type the application accepts; the content check
and the scanner then run as for any upload. A specific type the application does not accept stays
refused (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`): the extension never overrides it, and an extension of a
type the application does not accept names nothing. `text/xml` counts as such a type for `.xml`, whose
type is `application/xml`; an application that accepts `text/xml` but not `application/xml` keeps
receiving `text/xml`. Accept `text/csv` to take CSV exports; when the application also accepts
`application/vnd.ms-excel`, a `.csv` sent with that type still becomes `text/csv`. The
composer of `@newheap/platform-ai-chat` applies the same table before it uploads and declares the
type it derived.

The platform's table knows `.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`,
`.pptx`, `.doc`, `.xls`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.markdown`, `.json` and `.xml`. Map the
application's own extensions with `NhAssistantUploadOptions.MapExtension(extension, mediaType)`, such
as `.dwg` to `application/acad`: the derivation then uses the mapping exactly like the table, only while
the application accepts the mapped type, and a mapping of an extension the table knows takes
precedence over the table. `MapExtension` throws for an extension that is not a dot with letters,
digits, `_`, `+` or `-` (at most 32 characters), a value that is not a media type, or more than
`MaxMappedExtensions` (100) extensions. The agents' upload rules carry the mappings of accepted types
(`NhAssistantAgentUploadsDto.MappedExtensions`), so the composer derives alike and its file picker
offers the extensions. The sample maps `.jfif` to JPEG (SPM-305).

The content check also covers text: an upload whose type resolves to `text/*`, `application/json`,
`application/xml` or a `+json` or `+xml` type is refused (`assistant-file-type-not-accepted`) when its
content starts with the signature of an OLE2 compound file (Word, Excel or PowerPoint 97 to 2003), a
ZIP package, a PDF, or a PNG, JPEG or GIF image, such as an `.xls` workbook renamed to `.csv`. There is
no NUL-byte check, so UTF-16 text, such as Excel's "Unicode text" export, passes. A `.pptx` must start as
a ZIP package, as a `.docx` and an `.xlsx` must. Check the rest of the content of the text types the
application accepts in its scanner or file source.

```csharp
services.AddNewHeapAssistant(assistant => assistant
    // ...
    .UseFileSource<ProjectMediaFileSource>()
    .ConfigureUploads(uploads =>
    {
        // PDF, PNG, JPEG, Word and Excel by default; no types switches uploads off.
        uploads.AcceptMediaTypes(NhAiMediaTypes.Pdf, NhAiMediaTypes.Png, NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg);
        // An extension the platform's table does not know names an accepted type.
        uploads.MapExtension(".jfif", NhAiMediaTypes.Jpeg);
        // Confidential by default: the profile, or a fallback, must permit it.
        uploads.DefaultClassification = NhAiDataClassification.Confidential;
        // Every upload passes the application's scanner before the file source stores it.
        uploads.UseScanner<EicarUploadScanner>();
    }));
```

- A scanner (scoped) receives the checked upload and its actor and returns `TaskResult`: a failed
  result refuses the file, a failed result with `assistant-file-upload-failed` says the scan could not
  run. Its messages are never shown or logged. The sample's `EicarUploadScanner` (SPM-305) refuses
  the EICAR test string; a real application calls its virus scanner there.

- Store the classification of an upload with the file and report it from `OpenAsync`; raise it when
  the application knows the content is more sensitive. Uploads that no message ends up carrying stay
  in the application's storage under its own retention.
- Let uploads go with their conversation with `UseFileRetention<T>()`, where `T` implements
  `INhAssistantFileRetention`. The assistant calls `ForgetConversationAsync` with a
  `NhAssistantForgottenConversation` (the conversation, its agent and tenant, the subject of a thread
  and the reason, `archived` or `subject-forgotten` of `NhAssistantFileRetentionReasons`) after the
  owner's archive of a chat committed (`DELETE conversations/{id}`; a participant who leaves forgets
  nothing) and after `INhAiSubjectRetention.ForgetSubjectAsync` deleted each agent's thread. It is best
  effort: a failed result or an exception is logged as a warning with the conversation and the code or
  exception type, never undoes the archive or the deletion and is not retried. Make it idempotent, so
  that forgetting a conversation without uploads or one forgotten before succeeds and the
  application's own retention can call it again for one it missed. The sample's
  `ProjectMediaUploadRetention` (SPM-359) removes the conversation's upload folder from the media
  library.
- The endpoint lowers the request body limit of an upload to the agent's `MaxFileBytes` plus 16 KB,
  but never raises the server's own limit (Kestrel's `MaxRequestBodySize`, 30 MB by default); raise
  that one too when `MaxFileBytes` is larger.
- `GET status` and `GET agents` give each agent `uploads` (`NhAssistantAgentUploadsDto`) with the
  accepted media types, the largest file and the most files of one message, or `null` when people can
  attach nothing to it, so a client checks a file before it uploads it. An agent offers uploads only
  when its profile or a fallback permits, in the execution region, the classification a message with
  an upload carries: the higher of the agent's own and `DefaultClassification`. Otherwise `uploads` is
  `null` and an upload answers `409 assistant-files-not-accepted`, instead of an offered upload that
  the turn then refuses with `assistant-classification-not-permitted`. The sample's quick answers agent
  runs on a profile for internal data only and offers none (SPM-359).
- The conversation shows a person's attachments as `file` parts (`NhAssistantFilePartDto`) with name,
  media type and size, also in the live `message.created` event; never the content, the application's
  id or a hash. Files a tool returned stay named in that call's result, which follows the viewer's
  rights to it. A message with attachments in a busy agent thread waits for the next run with its
  files (`202` with the trigger receipt), unless the agent takes no files
  (`assistant-files-not-accepted`) or fewer (`assistant-file-count-limit`); the run opens them as
  attachments with the rights of the person who wrote the message, within the limits of the skill it
  works in, and a file it cannot open is named to the model with its code instead.

## Agent threads

An agent that runs on its own (see the agent-runs rule) keeps one thread per agent and
subject in the same `nhai` schema. A thread is a conversation of kind `thread`; it never
appears in a person's conversation list, and nobody owns it: the subject's access
resolver decides on every request who reads it, who types in it and who decides its
proposals. A person who types in a thread starts a turn in which that person is the
initiator; such a turn is bound to the request like a chat turn, its approvals are
always inline, and a message that arrives while a run is active waits for the next
run (`202 Accepted` with a receipt). Request-bound turns end with the request, and
their cancellation reaches only the process that runs them; work that must outlive a
request belongs in an agent run.

## Context for a reviewed MCP tool

When a remote service needs the conversation to answer, keep its model-facing schema
small (for example only `question`) and send the context as request metadata instead.
Register the reviewed tool in code with `AddMcpContextBinding(new
NhAssistantMcpContextBinding(serverId, serverUrl, remoteName))`. The binding applies
only while an administrator connects the server under that id and URL; any other
server, URL or tool never receives the context. Each call then carries `_meta` key
`com.newheap/assistant-context` with the acting agent, the accountable person, the
conversation, turn and tool invocation ids, the approval and proposal ids of an approved
call and, unless `IncludeSnapshot` is off, a bounded snapshot: the first question plus
the latest completed user and assistant text within `NhAssistantConversationSnapshotRequest`
(`MaxRecentMessages`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxMessageBytes`), with omitted messages and bytes.
Code that needs the snapshot elsewhere inside a tool call uses
`INhAssistantConversationSnapshotProvider` with the call's invocation context. It
verifies the running call, the run, the accountable actor's access and the active turn
itself, and never returns instructions, tool calls or results, approvals, page context
or output of the running turn, also not text written before an approval pause. A binding that
the application reviews and stores while it runs, instead of in code, follows "Links the
application stores" below.

## Reviewed imported MCP tools for a person's own AI app

Imported MCP tools never reach an MCP client by default. When people should call a coupled
application's read tools from their own AI app, without a turn of the assistant in between, opt in
with `ExportImportedMcpTools<TSelector>()` next to `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools` (SPM-399). The
scoped `INhAssistantImportedMcpToolExportSelector` is asked per request about each enabled tool
(`NhAssistantExportableMcpTool`: server, remote name, the reviewed description and effect)
of an enabled server whose credential belongs to the organization and whose required policy, or
else the assistant's access policy, the caller passes; it returns an `NhAssistantImportedMcpToolExport`
with the export name, or `null`. A tool is then imported for the calling person exactly as in that
person's own turn: with the server's own credential (a person's OAuth connection or a forwarded
token never serves the export), the reviewed description and the remote schema, skipped and, with the
shared credential, disabled when its schema no longer matches the reviewed one. The host's
`INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` must allow its `mcp.<server>.<tool>` id per caller, as the sample's
`ProjectAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` does for the research server. A call runs through `INhAiToolInvoker`
with the caller's invocation context and is audited there (`INhAiAuditSink`: tool id with server and
tool, the caller, the outcome); the assistant's business audit stays bound to turns. A tool with a
context binding receives `com.newheap/assistant-context` with `channel: mcp`, the caller as actor
and `accountableOwnerId` and no conversation, snapshot or chain, so the remote binds the call to the
person itself. A server that serves background runs with the organization's credential
(`headlessUse: organization`) acts for nobody in particular and is left out unless the selection sets
`AllowOrganizationHeadlessServer`. An export name holds 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores, dots or
dashes; one that another tool of the export has fails the listing.

A tool that changes something is exported only when the selection sets `ClientConfirmationIsApproval`:
the host declares that the person's AI app asks the person before each call and that this confirmation
is the approval. NewHeap offers it as destructive, so clients ask, and imports it with
consumer-authoritative approval and idempotency (part of its contract), which the invoker records as
`consumer-authoritative`; agents never get that contract. It needs a reviewed context binding, so the
remote learns the person, and otherwise is left out with `assistant-mcp-context-binding-required`. The
binding sends `idempotencyKey`: the key the client sent under `_meta` `com.newheap/idempotency-key`
(`NhAssistantMcpExportCall.IdempotencyKeyMetaKey`, at most 128 letters, digits, dots, colons,
underscores or dashes) so a retry carries the same key, or else one per call. The remote holds replays
against it, as its guards would against a conversation.

## Requests for input of MCP servers and approval pages for MCP clients

An administrator-connected MCP server may ask for input while its tool runs (MCP elicitation, SPM-251):
as a multi round-trip `input_required` result, as an `elicitation/create` request on the call's stream
of an older protocol revision, or by refusing the call with `URL_ELICITATION_REQUIRED` until a person
finished a page of its own. The assistant's client declares both modes and asks the person of the
governed call in a person's chat turn; nothing needs configuring. The chat shows the server's message
as the server's (`elicitation` part, `elicitation.requested` and `elicitation.closed` events,
`NhAssistantElicitationPartDto`), never to the model, with a form of strings, numbers, integers,
booleans and single choices (`NhAssistantElicitationFieldDto`) or an https link with its host that the
person opens themselves. Only that person answers, through
`POST conversations/{id}/elicitations/{elicitationId}/answer` (`NhAssistantAnswerElicitationRequest`);
the answer goes straight back to the waiting call, is checked against the fields and is never stored.
A finished page lets a refused call run again within the same governed execution; a cancelled one fails
it with `ai-mcp-url-elicitation-required`. The wait follows the tool's own timeout. Requests without a
person (a run, a consultation, a rule turn, a call of an exported tool), with nested or multiple-choice
values, more than eight fields, a message over 1,000 characters or a link that is not https are declined
without asking anyone. The audit records `McpElicitationRequested` and `McpElicitationClosed` with the
server, the call, the mode and the outcome, never the message or the answer.

Set `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:ApprovalLinkTemplate` (`NhAssistantMcpOptions.ApprovalLinkTemplate`, an
absolute https page with one `{approvalId}`, http only on a loopback name) to send an MCP client of
`WithNewHeapPlatformAITools` to the application's approval page when its call left proposals for a
person to decide, through `INhAssistantProposals.ProposeForAsync` or a consultation whose proposals
wait for the subject's approvers (SPM-364, SPM-370). A client that supports multi round-trip requests
and link requests receives `input_required` with a URL elicitation and a protected request state that
names only the proposals, the caller and the tool; its retry never runs the tool again, is checked for
the caller and returns the decision: approved and executed (`_meta` `newheap/approvals`), rejected
(`assistant-mcp-proposal-rejected`), closed (`assistant-mcp-proposal-closed`) or still pending
(`ai-tool-approval-required`), at most three rounds. A forged or foreign state fails with
`assistant-mcp-approval-state-invalid`. The decision stays on the page with the proposal's hash.

## Consultation chains across applications

When cooperating applications consult each other's agents over MCP, let them keep one
consultation chain, so a loop between them is refused as one host refuses it (SPM-366). Name
the application once with `UseMcpChainApplication(applicationId)`, for example its public origin
or token issuer: 1 to `NhAssistantMcpContext.MaxApplicationIdLength` characters without white
space or control characters (`IsApplicationId`). Every application of a chain needs a name of
its own.

On the sending side set `IncludeChain = true` on the `NhAssistantMcpContextBinding` of the other
application's consult tool. The assistant context then also carries `chain`: `agents`, the agents
that asked, outermost first and each as `{ "application", "agentId" }`, ending with the calling
turn's own agent, and `consultationDepth`, the depth of the calling turn (0 outside a
consultation). The version stays 1 and the other members keep their shape, so a receiver that does
not know `chain` reads the rest as before. A consultation turn offers no administrator-connected MCP
tools, so a consulted agent reaches another application through a code-owned import
(`INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`) whose policy names `InvocationBinderId =
NhAssistantMcpContext.BinderId` for the binding's server id and remote name. With the chain the
binding also binds a call from a consultation turn: its `conversation` names the consulted agent's
thread and the consultation as turn, and it carries no snapshot.

On the receiving side register every reviewed caller with `ContinueMcpChain(new
NhAssistantMcpChainCaller(applicationId, issuer))`. A request is from that caller when its
authenticated principal carries exactly one `IssuerClaimType` claim (`iss`) with the issuer and,
for an issuer that serves several applications, exactly one `ClientClaimType` claim with
`ClientId`. A consultation such a caller starts over MCP begins where its chain ended: one level
deeper than the deeper of the caller's depth and this application's own, with the caller's agents
counted as askers, each qualified by its application. `MaxConsultationDepth` then bounds the whole
path, and an agent of this application already in the chain, also on a path that never returns to
the application that asked first, refuses the call with `assistant-consult-depth-exceeded` before a
consultation is recorded or the agent runs. Two applications with an agent of the same id never
refuse each other. A request (`assistant.request.*`) whose chain comes from a consultation is
refused the same way, as one host never offers a request inside a consultation. The chain of any
other caller is ignored, never refused, so an ordinary MCP client keeps working: the call is a
direct call at depth 1. A malformed chain of a reviewed caller is ignored too, with a warning that
names the problem and not the payload: another version, a missing or non-integer depth, no agents
or more than `MaxChainAgents`, an invalid application or agent id, or a calling agent of another
application than the caller's. The consultation keeps `AskingAgentId` `null`, because no agent of
this application asked, and counts the chain in `Depth`.

The chain is loop protection between cooperating applications, not authorization. The caller's
person still needs the consultation's policy and a role on the subject, and the consulted agent's
daily `Budget`, `MaxConsultationsPerActorPerDay` and the call's deadline bound a caller that sends
no chain or a forged one: a forged shallow chain costs budget, never correctness.

## Links the application stores

`ContinueMcpChain` and `AddMcpContextBinding` are reviewed with the code and count from the next
start. When the application links applications while it runs, for example on an administrator screen
behind a permission and a review of its own, register an `INhAssistantMcpLinks` with
`UseMcpLinks<TLinks>()` next to the code registrations (FB59; SPM-266 and SPM-366). Its `ListAsync`
returns an `NhAssistantMcpLinkList`: the `ChainCallers` whose chains this application continues and
the `ContextBindings` of tools on administrator-connected servers, as the application reviewed and
stores them now. It is a scoped service that the assistant resolves in a scope of its own, never in a
person's request, so answer with the application's links and nothing that depends on the request. The
application owns who may create a link, as it owns approver candidates; NewHeap owns what a link may
do.

The assistant reads the source when a turn imports the tools of an administrator-connected server
that code does not bind, when it binds such a tool's call, and when an MCP call that carries a chain
starts a consultation. It reuses an answer for `NhAssistantMcpOptions.LinkCacheDuration`
(`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:LinkCacheDuration`, 30 seconds by default, from zero to 5 minutes) on the
application's clock, so a link the application adds or revokes counts within that time without a
restart; zero reads on every use. Code registrations never depend on the source and behave as
before.

NewHeap checks every stored entry exactly as it checks the same registration in code at startup and
leaves out an entry that registration would refuse. It logs a warning with the kind of entry, its
position, its application or server id when that is valid, and the reason
(`NhAssistantMcpLinkProblems`) when the reason first appears, not on every read: `entry-missing`,
`too-many-entries` (more than `NhAssistantMcpLinkList.MaxEntries` in a list), `application-id-invalid`,
`issuer-invalid`, `client-invalid`, `chain-application-missing` (a caller, or a binding with
`IncludeChain`, while the application has no name in chains), `own-application-name`,
`caller-conflict` (an issuer and client that code or another stored entry names as another
application), `server-url-invalid`, `tool-invalid`, `snapshot-invalid`, `code-binding` (code binds the
same server id and tool, and its binding applies) and `binding-conflict` (two different stored
bindings of one server id and tool, of which neither applies). A stored entry never grants more than
a registration could:

- A stored binding applies only to a tool of an administrator-connected server while the server keeps
  the binding's id and URL. A code-owned import (`INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`) still needs
  `AddMcpContextBinding`, and a consultation turn, which offers no administrator-connected tools, never
  uses a stored binding.
- A stored caller is believed only for a request whose authenticated principal carries exactly its
  issuer and, when it names one, its client. It is loop protection, as a registered caller is, never
  authorization.

A source that throws, or does not answer within `NhAssistantMcpLinkList.ReadTimeLimit` (10 seconds),
is logged with its type and the exception's type, never the message. Until the next read only the code
registrations count: stored links fail closed. The binder is part of a tool's contract, so adding or
revoking a stored binding changes the contract of that tool: a proposal of it that waits for a
decision no longer runs, and the model proposes it again. A call whose import applied a stored binding
that was revoked before the call is bound stops with `ai-mcp-binding-failed` instead of going out
without the context.

## Compositions and scripts: a switch the application owns

A composition runs a known chain of governed tools as one tool, and the script tool runs a short
program the model writes over the tools of its turn. Both mark their descriptor with
`NhAiToolDescriptor.CompositionFeature` (`NhAiCompositionFeature.Compositions` or `Scripts`); every
other tool keeps `None` and nothing below ever affects it. A marked tool is offered only where three
things allow it, decided once per feature at the start of each turn, run step and MCP request:

1. **Code** sets the ceiling. An agent in code opts in with
   `ConfigureAgentContext(agentId, c => c.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`. Agents created in the
   administration get them only within `UseCompositionsAsData(c => c.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`,
   and then each such agent carries its own `compositions` and `scripts` setting, saved and versioned
   with its definition, carried in agent packages only when on and taken over by a promoted shadow
   variant; switching on what the ceiling does not allow answers `compositions: not-allowed` or
   `scripts: not-allowed` (`NhAssistantFieldErrors.NotAllowed`), while a setting the agent already has
   stays accepted. An MCP exposure opts in with `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools(mcp => mcp.AllowCompositions().AllowScripts())`.
2. **The application's switch** decides at run time: `INhAssistantCompositionSwitch.IsOnAsync` with
   `NhAssistantCompositionSwitchContext` (the feature, the channel `Chat`, `Run`, `Consultation`,
   `HandOff` or `Mcp`, the tenant, the agent, `null` for MCP, and the person: the person who chats,
   a run's initiator, the person who asked a consultation, the MCP caller). The default reads
   `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Compositions` and `NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Scripts`, both off. An application
   that offers the features as a setting of its own registers `UseCompositionSwitch<TSwitch>()`, a
   scoped service that reads its own table with a cache of its own, because it is asked every turn.
   The switch is asked only where code allows the feature and a tool of it is registered; one that
   throws counts as off and only the exception type is logged.
3. **The tool** must be registered in a catalog (`Agent` exposure for agents, `Mcp` for the export).
   Compositions are selected by the agent's tool selectors like any tool; the script tool needs no
   selector, also not in a consultation's own selection, because the ceiling is its opt-in and a script
   only calls the tools its turn offers. Effect and autonomy rules still apply to both.

A value that changes during a turn applies from the next one, so a running script never flips halfway.
While a feature is off its tools are not offered to the model and not listed over MCP, and a call that
still arrives, such as an approved proposal of a composition or an MCP call from an earlier list, is
refused with `assistant-composition-off` or `assistant-scripting-off` before anything runs; a marked
tool the MCP exposure does not allow is not part of it (`ai-tool-not-authorized`).

`INhAssistantCompositionStatus.GetAsync` and `GET admin/agents/{id}/compositions` (administration
policy) return what the assistant actually does for one agent, per feature and per channel, and why
(`NhAssistantCompositionReasons`): `on`, `not-installed` (no tool of the feature; for scripts the
scripting package), `agent-not-allowed` (an agent in code), `not-allowed-for-data-agents` or
`off-for-agent` (an agent created in the administration) and `off-by-application`. The switch is asked
for the reading person and tenant. Show it next to the application's own checkbox, as the
administration's agent page does. The run catalog reports `compositionCeiling`. The sample stores its
setting per environment and agent in its own table and switches the project assistant and the scripting
desk, an agent created as data (SPM-371).

## Compositions and the step runtime

Declare a known chain of governed tools as one tool with `AddComposition<TInput>(id, ...)` when the
model would otherwise read every intermediate result to choose the next call (SPM-372). The steps
call registered tools by id, in order; a later step takes values from earlier results through
`NhAssistantCompositionContext<TInput>.Result`, and `Returns` declares the only data that reaches the
model. Prefer a composition over a hand-written `[NhAiTool]` that calls services directly: that tool
loses per-step rights, approval, guards, budget and audit.

```csharp
assistant.AddComposition<ProjectOverviewInput>("projects.overview", composition => composition
    .Describe("Show one project with its open tasks and its members in one call.")
    .ExposeOverMcp()
    .Step("project", "projects.get", context => new { projectId = context.Input.ProjectId })
    .Step("open-tasks", "projects.list-open-tasks", context => new
    {
        projectId = context.Result("project").GetProperty("id").GetGuid()
    })
    .Returns(context => new { project = context.Result("project"), openTasks = context.Result("open-tasks") }));
```

- The composition is a tool marked `NhAiCompositionFeature.Compositions`. Its effect is the strongest
  effect of its steps and its classification the highest, so one that only reads runs at once and is
  read-only over MCP. An agent's tool selectors select it where code allows compositions
  (`ConfigureAgentContext(...).AllowCompositions()`) and the application's switch has them on, and a
  turn offers it only together with every tool its steps call. With `ExposeOverMcp` an exposure that
  allows compositions lists it; its steps must be exposed there too.
- Every step runs through the shared invoker with the caller's context and gets exactly the decision
  the same call gets on its own. A `Deferred` proposal returns the usual "proposal recorded" result and
  the chain continues; a later step that reads its result stops the chain with
  `assistant-composition-step-result-unavailable`. An `Inline` approval stops the chain, the turn
  waits as it does for a call of the model, and after the decision the model reads its own call, where
  the chain stopped, and the decided step. A shadow run proposes every change and executes none. A step
  that fails or is refused stops the chain; the model receives what succeeded and that step's code.
- Steps never call another composition, the script tool, a consultation or a destructive tool, and a
  step's files are not opened: return what the model needs through `Returns`.
- Over MCP, and for any caller outside a turn, a step runs through its governed function: a step that
  needs approval fails with `ai-tool-approval-required`, as the same call does there.
- The steps' tools are read once, at startup, from the tool catalogs of a scope of their own, so a
  catalog registered as a scoped service, such as one that holds the tools a run imported, works next to
  compositions, also where the host validates scopes, as Development does. A step's tool must not depend
  on the request: a step calls only a tool that a scope without a request has too, and a catalog whose
  descriptors change while the host runs implements `INhAiChangingToolCatalog`, which compositions leave
  out; a step that names another tool stops the host. When a step runs, its tool comes from the turn's
  own services, never from that startup scope.

The step runtime is public for the script tool and for an application's own chain tool: from inside
the tool's governed function call `INhAssistantToolSteps.BeginAsync` with an
`NhAssistantToolStepRequest` (`MaxSteps`, `MaxMutationSteps`, `Hash`, `Tools`), run each step with
`NhAssistantToolStepSession.RunAsync`, stop when a step's `NhAssistantToolStepStatus` says so or the
session is `Stopped`, and call `CompleteAsync` once with the result the model receives. In a turn a step
may call only a tool the agent is offered in that turn; outside a turn only a tool the caller may
discover through the same exposure. Each step is a tool invocation of the turn whose call id names the
call that ran it; the message shows one card for the call, the first step uses its count of the turn's
tool calls and every further step counts as a call of its own. Every step's context, audit record and
proposal guard context carry `NhAiToolCallOrigin` (see the protected-actions rule).

The agent's Activity in the administration shows each composition and script call with the tool calls
it ran in order, the model rounds it saved (its tool calls minus one) and the size of the result
returned to the model, and per tool what the calls saved: `GET admin/agents/{id}/compositions/activity`
(`NhAssistantCompositionActivityDto`), `getAgentCompositionActivity` and the Compositions view of
`nh-assistant-agent-composition-activity`. It reads the stored tool invocations and is content-free;
calls in a consultation store nothing and are not listed.

## Avoid

- Exporting imported MCP tools by registering them as MCP-exposed catalogs or a second MCP client in
  the host; use `ExportImportedMcpTools`, which keeps the turn's credential, binding, bounds and audit.
  Do not allow a server that serves background runs with the organization's credential in the export
  unless that server binds each call to the person itself.
- Setting `ClientConfirmationIsApproval` for a client that runs tools without asking the person, or
  for a remote that ignores `idempotencyKey`; the confirmation is the only approval such a change gets.
- Treating an MCP server's request for input as the assistant's or the model's text, opening its link
  for the person, storing the answer, or treating an MCP client's accepted elicitation as an approval;
  a proposal is decided on the application's page with its hash.

- Treating a chat about a subject as the agent's thread, or authorizing a tool on
  `ConversationSubject` alone: it names what the person asked about, and the tool still checks the
  person's own rights. Do not cache a person's role on the chat's subject; the assistant asks the
  resolver on every turn, read and invitation so that a revoked role takes effect at once.
- Calling `AddNewHeapAssistant` before `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet` or replacing the
  invocation gate, budget, idempotency or evidence manager afterwards; startup fails.
- Believing a consultation chain from a caller you did not review with `ContinueMcpChain`, or
  reading the chain as authorization; it only ever refuses, and budgets and limits still bound a
  forged one.
- Giving two applications of a chain the same name, or reviewing a caller under this application's
  own name: agents of the same id would refuse each other, and startup refuses the second. A binding
  with `IncludeChain` or a reviewed caller without `UseMcpChainApplication` fails startup too.
- Answering `INhAssistantMcpLinks` with anything of the person or request in scope, or letting anyone
  store a link without the application's own permission and review: the assistant reads it in a scope
  of its own and shares the answer with every request for `LinkCacheDuration`.
- Expecting a stored binding to bind a code-owned import, or a stored entry to replace a code
  registration: code-owned imports keep their code binding, and a server id and tool or an issuer and
  client that code registers keep their code registration.
- Registering or replacing `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` for the assistant; discovery
  stays owned by the application or the API bridge.
- Offering a composition or the script tool as an extra function outside a tool catalog, or reading
  the application's setting yourself in a tool: only marked catalog tools follow the switch, the
  ceiling and the refusal codes. Do not read a database without a cache in
  `INhAssistantCompositionSwitch`; it is asked every turn.
- Adding agent-specific copies of tools to bypass approval, or approving on behalf
  of the user from code.
- Letting an impersonation session record a personal grant of the impersonated person, such as
  background-use consent, a personal MCP connection or a push subscription, in an endpoint of your
  own; refuse it as the assistant does with `assistant-not-allowed-while-impersonating` and keep
  withdrawals open.
- Issuing a channel credential, such as a messaging link token, from an impersonation session, binding
  it to nothing but the person's id, or renewing it with a full lifetime from itself; it would act as
  the person after the impersonation, the password change or the revocation that should end it.
- Writing prompts, messages, tool arguments or results to logs, `INhAiAuditSink`,
  usage records or `INhAssistantBusinessAuditSink`; those receive identifiers,
  versions, codes and timestamps only.
- Applying the library migrations to a shared database without an explicit
  deployment decision; `RunMigrations` is off by default.
- Relying on `POST cancel` across nodes; it reaches turns in the same process, and
  an abandoned running turn is recovered after its deadline.
- Starting a person's turn from a channel by calling the application's own assistant endpoints with
  a service credential, or by authorizing tools against the channel's request; use
  `INhAssistantConversationTurns`, whose tools authorize the person it names. Never pass a principal
  the application did not authenticate as that person.
- Expecting `KeepTurnsAfterDisconnect` to resume a stream; the client reloads the conversation.
- Reading the turn's person from `IHttpContextAccessor` in a tool, policy or turn context provider; a
  channel's turn and a turn that outlived its request have no request of the person. Inject
  `INhAiTurnPerson`.
- Polling `INhAssistantConversations.GetAsync` for the end of a turn; use
  `INhAssistantConversationTurns.WaitAsync`.
- Assuming a server's tools wait for the slowest server: an agent's MCP servers connect at the same
  time and their tools keep one order, so the list the model reads stays the same from turn to turn.
- Calling the endpoints to create, list, read, stop or answer a person's chat, list their agents or
  upload a file from a channel; use `INhAssistantConversations` and
  `INhAssistantConversationTurns.AnswerAsync`. Implementing or mocking `INhAssistantConversations`
  outside the application's own tests: it grows with the endpoints.
- Passing the page a person has open from a channel through a turn context provider of the channel's
  own; pass it as `NhAssistantConversationMessage.ClientContext`, which the turn shows as the person's
  screen and stores like the endpoint.
- Keeping a channel's own table of assistant codes to HTTP statuses; map the application's own codes,
  then `NhAssistantHttpStatuses.Of(code)`.
- Passing a forward-only stream to `UploadAsync`, or logging the name of an upload in a scanner, file
  source or file retention.
- Trusting remote MCP annotations such as `readOnlyHint`; they are hints for the
  administrator only. Mark a remote tool read-only only after reviewing it.
- Forwarding user tokens to hosts outside `ForwardUserTokenHosts`, or allowing plain
  http, link-local or metadata addresses for MCP servers.
- Writing MCP server, tool or assignment rows from application code, or calling the administration's
  endpoints from the application's own backend; use `INhAssistantMcpServers`, which keeps the checks,
  secrets and audit. Turning `AllowLoopback` on outside test hosts.
- Setting `headlessUse` to `organization` for a server whose credential lets an agent
